A first stop before [Classic Synths Compared](synth-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the MS-20 is and when it was made.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Find records it is on.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **MS-20** was made by **Korg** and released in **1978** (Wikipedia, "Korg MS-20").
- It is monophonic and **semi-modular**: it works without cords, and a **patch panel** changes it (MS-20 manual, pp. 6-7).
- Wikipedia: its "flexibility led to its resurgence during the analog revival of the late 1990s."

## Its sound

- **Two filters in a row**: a high-pass, then a low-pass (MS-20 manual, p. 5).
- Each has a **Peak** knob that goes up to self-oscillation, so the filters scream (manual, p. 5).
- VCO-2 can be a **ring modulator** for bells and clangs (manual, p. 5).
- Two envelope generators: EG 1 (delay, attack, release) and EG 2 (hold, attack, decay, sustain, release) (manual, pp. 6-7).

## The panel

This is the MS-20 panel from [Classic Synths Compared](synth-compare.qmd), drawn after the real one (not a copy). Play it from the keys under the panel, the computer keys (a w s e d f t g y h u j k) or a MIDI keyboard. Turn any knob while you play. The sound is this site's own model; nobody has compared it with the real instrument.

## Guided tour

Each step loads a worked example and changes one thing.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="ms20-hot" data-set="{&quot;hPeak&quot;:0,&quot;lPeak&quot;:0,&quot;hCut&quot;:0}"><p><b>Both peaks at 0.</b> A plain sawtooth through the filters. Listen: an ordinary lead.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="ms20-hot" data-set="{&quot;hPeak&quot;:0,&quot;hCut&quot;:0}"><p><b>Low-pass Peak up.</b> The <b>low-pass Peak</b> to 8. Listen for a loud whistle on top.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="ms20-hot" data-set="{&quot;hPeak&quot;:0}"><p><b>High-pass cutoff up.</b> The <b>high-pass</b> cuts the low end away. Listen: thinner.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="ms20-hot"><p><b>High-pass Peak up too.</b> Both peaks high. Listen: the MS-20 scream.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="ms20-ring"><p><b>The ring modulator.</b> VCO-2 on ring, with EG 1 sweeping the pitch. Listen for clanging bells.</p></div>
```

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>The MS-20&#x27;s two filters are…</b></p><ul><li>High-pass then low-pass</li><li>Two reverbs</li><li>Two drums</li><li>Two keyboards</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual p. 5.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What does turning Peak right up do?</b></p><ul><li>The filter whistles by itself</li><li>The sound stops</li><li>It plays chords</li><li>It slows down</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Self-oscillation.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Where do patch cords go on the MS-20?</b></p><ul><li>The patch panel</li><li>The keyboard</li><li>The battery</li><li>Nowhere</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual pp. 6-7.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="1"><p><b>Which year did the MS-20 come out?</b></p><ul><li>1958</li><li>1978</li><li>2008</li><li>1998</li></ul><p class="ik-why">1978.</p></div>
```

**For students**

Korg. *MS-20 Owner's Manual*. Keio Electronic Laboratories, 1978, [www.korg.com/us/support/download/manual/0/131/2441/](https://www.korg.com/us/support/download/manual/0/131/2441/). VCOs, waveforms and ring modulator, high-pass and low-pass filters with peak up to self-oscillation (p. 5); EG 1, EG 2 with hold, MG, the patch panel (pp. 6-7). A scan, read by OCR.

**For teachers**

"Korg MS-20." *Wikipedia*, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korg_MS-20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korg_MS-20). 1978-1983, monophonic, semi-modular, high-pass and low-pass filters in series; the 2014 kit's two filter types.
:::
